## Personality

Jane is a plain, steady, and conscientious individual known for her sensible, lady-like, and practical nature. Dutiful and strict in her conduct, she finds teaching somewhat monotonous due to how firmly she disciplines her pupils. She is motivated to earn her salary fairly, please the school trustees, and earn a spot on the School Inspector's roll of honor, intending to devote her entire life to teaching rather than marriage.

## History

[Jane Andrews](../character/jane-andrews.md) joined [Anne](../character/anne.md) Shirley's newly formed story club alongside [Ruby Gillis](../character/ruby-gillis.md) and other school friends, avoiding any mention of lovemaking in her written pieces because reading it aloud made her feel silly. After preparing for higher education in the special entrance class, Jane successfully passed the entrance examinations for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) and attended the school along with her [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) classmates. Following their time at Queen's, she joined [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Diana Barry](../character/di.md), and [Priscilla Grant](../character/priscilla-grant.md) on a spring outing into the woods, where they discovered [Hester](../character/hester-gray.md) Gray's hidden garden, shared a picnic by a brook, and discussed romantic stories and poetry. During a meeting of the Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society), Jane accompanied [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) to plead with [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) to stop him from renting his fences for medicine advertisements, though Parker initially refused their request. As her friends prepared for future pursuits, local gossip continued to circulate regarding Jane and her peers.

## Quotes

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers. “Oh, Anne I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
>
> — Jane — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)

> "Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful."
>
> — Jane — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> "Even Levi Boulter or Lorenzo White would never stoop to that, tightfisted as they are. They would have too much respect for public opinion."
>
> — Jane — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P57](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0057)

> "I can’t understand how she could have wanted to live back here, away from everything,"
>
> — Jane — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P55](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0055)
